# R0 — Editor’s + Author’s Prefaces (lines 235–259)

**Range read in full:** 235–259  
**Source:** Cockerill, *The Epistle to the Hebrews* (NICNT, 2012)  
**Evidence class default:** Fee (editor) or Cockerill (author) as marked.

## Claims

### C1 — Fee: replaces Bruce; final editorial task; pastoral audience
**Locus:** 235  
**Quote:** "this work represents a signal end of an era for this commentary series, since it is both replacing a commentary by the second general editor (F. F. Bruce) and is the final editorial task of the third general editor, whose onsetting bout with Alzheimer's disease has necessitated his relinquishing this task"  
**Claim:** (Fee) Cockerill’s volume replaces F. F. Bruce’s NICNT Hebrews; Fee’s last editorial task due to Alzheimer’s; primary audience “busy pastor” and college/seminary students; Fee worked closely with “Gary Cockerill.”

### C2 — Cockerill: pastoral-transformative aim (Hays)
**Locus:** 243  
**Quote:** "I would enable modern readers to enter the Christian world of Hebrews and allow that world to reshape their hearts and minds… Richard Hays has reminded the church that the purpose of biblical exposition is to enter the biblical narrative and allow it to transform the hearer's perspective and behavior."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Commentary aims beyond laboratory explication: hear God’s word in the Son, enter divine presence through cleansing, persevere in obedient faithfulness; methodologically aligned with Hays’s narrative-transformative exposition.

### C3 — Justification for new NICNT: rhetoric, discourse analysis, intertextuality
**Locus:** 245  
**Quote:** "I suggested that developments over the past decades in the study of ancient rhetoric, in the analysis of Hebrews' structure (particularly through discourse analysis), and in intertextual studies warranted such a venture."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill to Fee) Three warrant-fields for replacing Bruce: ancient rhetoric, structural/discourse analysis, intertextual OT studies; Hebrews is most diligent NT book in presenting OT Scripture and has unmatched rhetorical sophistication.

### C4 — Fresh structural/rhetorical analysis governs every passage
**Locus:** 247  
**Quote:** "this commentary is based on a fresh analysis of the structure and rhetorical shape of Hebrews. Each individual passage is interpreted with sensitivity to the role it plays within the author's overall strategy for persuading his hearers"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Signature method: structural-rhetorical whole; reader should engage Introduction’s structure before favorite passages; judge analysis by enrichment of individual passages and whole.

### C5 — OT hermeneutic: continuity and fulfillment
**Locus:** 249  
**Quote:** "The author of Hebrews understands the relationship between God's word in the Son and previous revelation as one of continuity and fulfillment."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Load-bearing OT-use category is continuity-and-fulfillment; Introduction’s OT section governs exposition proper.

### C6 — Authorship/destination agnosticism as methodological control
**Locus:** 251  
**Quote:** "the evidence available is insufficient to determine with certainty the name of the author or to be overly precise about the location, specific identity, and situation of the recipients. Thus those who base their interpretation on an unduly specific reconstruction of Hebrews' origin are likely to skew their understanding of the book in proportion to the idiosyncrasy of their proposal."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Refuses firm author-name and over-precise recipient reconstruction; surveys proposals for insight, not adjudication; over-specific origin hypotheses skew interpretation.

### C7 — Own translation; selective text-criticism; O'Brien in time, Allen late
**Locus:** 253  
**Quote:** "I have done my own translation of Hebrews… I have addressed textual issues only when they significantly impact interpretation… I am glad that the fine commentary by Peter O'Brien appeared just in time for consideration. I regret that my friend David Allen's commentary came just a bit too late."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Running text is his translation (not a fixed English version under critique); text-critical notes only when interpretive; secondary literature selective/comprehensive-as-possible; O’Brien consulted; Allen too late for engagement.

### C8 — Institutional and mentor provenance
**Locus:** 255  
**Quote:** "I am indebted to Professor Fee… That feedback set the direction for the whole… my doctoral mentor, Professor Mathias Rissi… first sparked my academic interest in Hebrews… Wesley Biblical Seminary… Reformed Theological Seminary, Jackson, Mississippi"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Fee’s feedback on opening chapters set whole direction; Rissi as doctoral mentor (commentary is not the one Rissi would have written); WBS institutional home; RTS Jackson library research support; dedication to wife Rosa, family, Dave Steveline (257).

## Coverage
Read lines 235–259 complete. No body commentary in this range. Suggested targets: `cockerill-hebrews-nicnt`, `gareth-lee-cockerill`, `f-f-bruce`, `hebrews`.
